question: A 43-year-old man with sexually acquired HIV infection (CD4 count 37 cells/mm3) presents with painless, progressive visual impairment. Funduscopy reveals yellow-white, fluffy retinal lesions near the retinal vessels with associated hemorrhage. Which of the following medications is the best initial therapy for this patient?
explanation: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis is the most common cause of ocular disease in patients with untreated AIDS and CD4 counts <50/mm3. The diagnosis is typically made by funduscopy, which reveals yellow-white, fluffy retinal lesions near the retinal vessels with associated hemorrhage. Ganciclovir is the first-line therapy for CMV retinitis.
